question.title: Will Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov visit Florida in December 2026?

research:
## Web research
**Briefing: Will Lavrov visit Florida between Dec 1 and Dec 31, 2026?**

**1. Current status (as of Nov 24, 2026): undecided. The criteria are not yet met.**
- **Summit.** The G20 leaders' summit is set for 14–15 December 2026 in Miami, Florida. The venue is Trump National Doral Miami, in Doral.
- **Russia's attendance (Nov 24).** Russian Foreign Ministry Ambassador-at-Large Marat Berdyev told Izvestia that Russia will be represented at the G20 summit in Miami and has yet to decide who will serve on its delegation. He said Russia will attend and will be represented at a high level. He did not name the delegation head.
- **Putin (Nov 24).** Peskov said "No. A decision hasn't been made yet," when asked whether Putin would attend. On Nov 18, Peskov said the decision would depend on many factors, including the outcome of Putin's talks with US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen.
- **Shenzhen meeting.** One low-quality aggregator (World Today News) reports that Trump, Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen and that Putin has been invited and Xi is almost certain to attend the Miami summit. I could not verify the Shenzhen meeting or its outcome from a primary source.
- **US invitation.** Rubio said on September 23, 2026 that the US had invited Putin, after meeting Lavrov at the UN. In April, Deputy FM Pankin said Russia has been invited to participate at the highest level. In March, Peskov said Putin does not plan to attend the G20 in Miami. That position has since softened to "no decision".
- **Lavrov's own comment (Oct 30–31).** At the Atlanta foreign ministers' meeting, Lavrov declined to say whether Putin will attend the G20 summit this December. He has not said whether he personally will go.

**2. Resolution source.** No specific source is named beyond "credible sources". Nothing yet reports Lavrov in Florida in December. Russian MFA and TASS statements and wire reports would be the primary evidence.

**3. Base rate**
- Lavrov led Russia's delegation when Putin skipped the 2022 Bali summit. Peskov and the Foreign Ministry confirmed Lavrov would head the delegation instead of Putin.
- For the 2023 New Delhi summit, Lavrov again led the delegation (from memory; I did not verify it in this search).
- Lavrov has just attended the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta. He arrived in Atlanta on Oct 30, so he has recently travelled to the US for a G20 event despite visa difficulties. The Russian foreign ministry complained that visa issues were only resolved at the last minute.
- If Putin attends, Lavrov would almost certainly accompany him. Lavrov travelled with Putin to the Alaska summit in August 2025 (from memory).
- If Putin skips, Lavrov is the most likely "high-level" representative. Alternatives are Deputy PM Overchuk, Finance Minister Siluanov, or Putin aide Ushakov (my inference; Berdyev named no one). Siluanov attended the G20 finance meetings, and allies succeeded in getting him excluded from a family photo.
- Lavrov has attended every G20 leaders' summit that Putin skipped since 2022 (my recollection, not checked).

**4. Scheduled events that could change the outcome**
- **Dec 14–15:** the Miami/Doral summit itself.
- **Before the summit:** a Kremlin announcement of the delegation. It will probably come close to the date, as in Bali and Delhi.
- **Ongoing:** US–Russia–Ukraine talks and the energy and diesel deals. Peskov tied the decision to the Putin–Trump talks in Shenzhen. Fresh Moscow–Kyiv–Washington talks were also expected, per an Oct 30 report.
- **Visa issues.** Visa friction was resolved only at the last minute for Atlanta and could recur.
- **European pushback.** European diplomats boycotted the Atlanta family photo, but this has not stopped Lavrov travelling.

**5. Prediction markets.** I found no market or forecaster numbers on Putin's or Lavrov's Miami attendance. I did not search Polymarket or Metaculus directly.

**6. Evidence on each side**

*Toward Yes:*
- Russia has said it will attend "at a high level" (Nov 24).
- Lavrov is the usual delegation head, or the usual companion if Putin goes.
- He has just travelled to the US for G20 ministerial work.
- The US is actively courting Russian participation and invited Putin personally.
- Russia wants sanctions and visa restrictions removed, and the MFA linked that work to the Miami summit.

*Toward No:*
- The delegation head is undecided, so it could be someone else, such as Overchuk or Siluanov, or Putin with a smaller entourage.
- Peskov said in March that Putin did not plan to attend. The Kremlin prefers Moscow for any Zelenskyy meeting.
- Visa and sanction obstacles and European hostility remain.
- Russia could downgrade its delegation or participate only virtually. Putin joined one G20 session virtually in 2023.
- The summit is only three weeks away, with the decision still pending.
- Lavrov has been described as travelling to NATO states only infrequently. That reflects sanctions and diplomatic friction, though he has just visited Atlanta.
- Lavrov could attend only a preparatory meeting outside Florida (none is known).

slots.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** The window runs from Dec 1 to Dec 31, 2026, so the outcome will be known within about five weeks. The key event is the G20 summit in Miami/Doral on Dec 14–15, roughly three weeks away.

**(b) Status quo:** Lavrov is not in Florida, and no trip has been announced. Russia has said it will attend the summit "at a high level" but has not named a delegation head. If nothing changes, this resolves No, though a scheduled event with confirmed Russian participation makes the status quo less sticky than usual.

**(c) No scenario:** Putin skips Miami and the Kremlin sends someone else, such as Oreshkin, Overchuk or Siluanov. As I recall, Oreshkin rather than Lavrov led the delegation to the 2025 Johannesburg summit, so Lavrov is not automatic. Visa trouble, a diplomatic flare-up, health (he is 76), or a downgrade to virtual participation could also keep him away.

**(d) Yes scenario:** Either Putin attends after positive talks with Trump and Lavrov accompanies him, as he did in Alaska in 2025, or Putin stays home and Lavrov leads the delegation, as in Bali 2022 and Delhi 2023 (and, as I recall, Rio 2024). Landing at a Miami airport is enough to resolve Yes.

**Rationale:** I split this by whether Putin attends.

- **Putin attends (about 30%):** The Kremlin has softened from "does not plan to attend" in March to "no decision" now, and the US has invited him personally. If he goes, Lavrov almost certainly accompanies him (about 90%).
- **Putin skips (about 70%):** Lavrov is the single most likely delegation head, and he just travelled to Atlanta for the G20 foreign ministers' meeting, which shows that he can and will go to the US. But the 2025 precedent and the Foreign Ministry's failure to name him three weeks out suggest real uncertainty. I put his chance at roughly 50%.

That gives about 0.27 + 0.35 = 0.62. I shade down slightly for visa friction, health, last-minute geopolitical disruption, and the pull of the status quo.

Probability: 59%

(a) Time left: the window runs December 1–31, 2026, so the outcome will be known within about five weeks. In practice it will be known by December 14–15, when the Miami summit takes place.

(b) Status quo: Lavrov is not in Florida and no trip has been announced. Russia has said it will attend "at a high level" but has not named a delegation head. If nothing changes, the answer is No, though a scheduled event makes a change plausible.

(c) No scenario: Putin skips Miami and the Kremlin sends someone else, as it did for Johannesburg in 2025, when I recall Maxim Oreshkin led the delegation rather than Lavrov. Alternatives include Oreshkin, Overchuk or Siluanov. Visa friction, a downgraded or virtual presence, or a breakdown in US–Russia talks could also keep Lavrov away.

(d) Yes scenario: Putin attends after a positive Trump meeting and Lavrov accompanies him, or Putin skips and Lavrov leads the delegation as he did in Bali (2022), New Delhi (2023) and Rio (2024). Either way he lands in Miami around December 13–15 and TASS or the Foreign Ministry reports it.

Rationale: I split this by whether Putin attends.

- **Putin attends (about 25%):** The Kremlin has softened from "does not plan to attend" in March to "no decision" now, and the US has invited him personally. If he goes, Lavrov very likely travels with him (about 90%).
- **Putin skips (about 75%):** Lavrov is the most likely head of delegation, but not a lock. The 2025 precedent shows the Kremlin will send an economic official instead. On the other hand, the US is hosting and courting Russia, and Lavrov just attended the Atlanta ministerial, which favours him. I put this at roughly 50%.

That gives about 0.25 × 0.9 + 0.75 × 0.5 ≈ 60%. I shade down slightly for visa problems, a possible last-minute downgrade and the fact that nothing is confirmed three weeks out. A non-G20 reason for Lavrov to be in Florida in December adds very little.

Probability: 56%

## OUTSIDE VIEW

**Reference class:** who represents Russia at G20 leaders' summits since 2022, when Putin stopped attending in person.

**Base rate:**
- 2022 Bali: Lavrov led the delegation (confirmed in the research).
- 2023 New Delhi: Lavrov led (assistant's recollection, consistent with mine).
- 2024 Rio: Lavrov led (my recollection).
- 2025 Johannesburg: I recall Maxim Oreshkin, deputy head of the presidential administration, leading, with Lavrov absent. This contradicts the assistant's unchecked claim that Lavrov attended every summit Putin skipped.

That gives roughly 3 of 4, or about 75%, for Lavrov being physically present. A US-hosted summit adds extra friction (visas, sanctions, politics), though Lavrov has travelled to the US regularly for UN meetings and, in this timeline, to Atlanta in October.

**Outside-view forecast:** about 60–65%. This is the 75% base rate discounted for the most recent summit breaking the pattern and for US-specific hurdles.

## INSIDE VIEW

(a) **Time left:** The summit is 14–15 December, about three weeks away. The window closes 31 December, about five weeks away.

(b) **Status quo:** Russia has said it will attend "at a high level" but has not named a delegation head. Putin is undecided. Lavrov has not been confirmed. If nothing changed, a Russian delegation goes to Miami, with Lavrov the single most likely member but not certain.

(c) **No scenario:** Putin stays home and the Kremlin sends Oreshkin, Overchuk, Dmitriev or Siluanov, as it did with Oreshkin in 2025. Other routes to No are a visa or political snag, a downgrade to virtual participation, or a summit disruption.

(d) **Yes scenario:** Putin skips and Lavrov leads the delegation as in 2022–2024, or Putin attends after a Trump deal and Lavrov accompanies him. Either way he lands in Miami around 13–15 December.

**Evidence adjustments:**
- **Russia confirms high-level attendance (Nov 24):** a small move up. It removes the "Russia doesn't show" branch, and "high level" fits Lavrov or Putin better than a sherpa.
- **Lavrov attended the Atlanta ministerial (Oct 30):** a moderate move up. It shows he is the active G20 face this year, visas can be resolved, and he is not sidelined as was rumoured in 2025.
- **Putin undecided, softened from "does not plan":** a slight move up. I put Putin attending at about 20%, and Lavrov would accompany him about 90% of the time.
- **Delegation "yet to be decided" three weeks out:** a small move down. If Lavrov were the default, it would be easy to say so. The Kremlin economic bloc (Oreshkin, Dmitriev) has been prominent in US–Russia dealings, and the 2025 precedent shows substitution is real.
- **Visa friction and European hostility:** a slight move down. These did not stop the Atlanta trip.
- **Other Florida visits in December (e.g., side talks):** negligible addition.

**Combining:** P(Putin attends) ≈ 0.2 × 0.9 = 0.18. P(Putin skips) ≈ 0.8 × 0.55 (Lavrov leads or joins) = 0.44. The total is about 62%.

Probability: 62%

**(a) Time left:** The summit is December 14–15, 2026, about three weeks away. The question window closes December 31, so the outcome will almost certainly be known by mid-December.

**(b) Status quo:** Lavrov is not in Florida, and no delegation head has been named. Russia has committed to attend "at a high level," so the status-quo trajectory is attendance by a senior figure. That figure may or may not be Lavrov.

**(c) No scenario:** Putin skips Miami. The Kremlin repeats its Johannesburg 2025 approach, when Maxim Oreshkin of the presidential administration led the delegation instead of Lavrov, and sends Oreshkin, Overchuk or Siluanov. Alternatively, a breakdown in Ukraine talks or last-minute visa or sanctions friction leads Russia to downgrade or join virtually.

**(d) Yes scenario:** Lavrov flies into Miami for the December 14–15 summit, in one of two ways.
- **Putin attends** after the US invitation and the Shenzhen talks, and Lavrov accompanies him, as he did in Alaska in 2025.
- **Putin stays home** and Lavrov heads the delegation, as in Bali 2022, New Delhi 2023 and Rio 2024.

**Rationale**

The case for Yes:
- Russia has publicly committed to high-level representation.
- The US host is actively courting Moscow and personally invited Putin.
- Lavrov travelled to the US just weeks ago for the Atlanta G20 foreign ministers' meeting. That shows visa issues are surmountable and his standing is intact.
- If Putin attends, Lavrov's presence is close to certain. I put the chance of Putin attending at perhaps 30–35%, given the softening from "no plans" to "no decision."
- If Putin doesn't go, Lavrov is the most likely delegation head, but not overwhelmingly so.

The case for No:
- The 2025 Johannesburg summit broke the pattern: Oreshkin led the delegation, not Lavrov. The briefing missed this.
- Delegation decisions often come late.
- Visa friction is recurring.
- A Trump-hosted summit, though, raises the stakes relative to South Africa, which favours a heavier hitter like Lavrov.

**Estimate:** Roughly 0.33 × 0.95 (Putin attends) + 0.67 × 0.55 (Putin skips) ≈ 0.31 + 0.37 ≈ 0.68. I shade that down slightly for visa problems, downgrade risk and possible virtual participation.

Probability: 63%

**(a) Time left:** The summit is December 14–15, 2026, about three weeks away. The question window closes December 31, so the answer will almost certainly be known by mid-December.

**(b) Status quo:** Lavrov is not in Florida, and nothing yet confirms he will go. But the status quo trajectory is that Russia attends "at a high level" (Berdyev, Nov 24). Lavrov is the default senior diplomat for that role.

**(c) No scenario:** Putin skips, and the Kremlin sends someone else, as it did at Johannesburg in 2025. There, Maxim Oreshkin, deputy head of the presidential administration, led the delegation instead of Lavrov. The substitute this time could be Oreshkin, Overchuk or Siluanov. Other routes to No:

**(d) Yes scenario:** One route is that Putin attends after the Shenzhen talks and Lavrov accompanies him to Doral, as he did in Alaska in 2025. The other is that Putin skips and Lavrov heads the delegation, as in Bali 2022, New Delhi 2023 and Rio 2024. Either way, Lavrov lands at Miami on or around December 13–15.

**Rationale:**

Against that, Lavrov appears fully active in 2026: he met Rubio at the UN in September and attended the Atlanta G20 foreign ministers' meeting in late October. Atlanta also shows that US visas can be obtained, if late. I put Lavrov's chances in this branch at about 55–60%.
- **Discounts:** I reduce the total slightly for visa and sanction friction, for the possibility of a virtual-only or downgraded presence, and for the decision still being open.

Combined: about 0.35×0.87 + 0.65×0.57 ≈ 0.67, discounted to roughly 0.60–0.63.

Probability: 61%

Or visa or political friction, or a breakdown in US–Russia talks, leads Russia to downgrade its attendance or join virtually. Lavrov could also skip the summit if Putin is absent and the Kremlin judges a Miami trip at Trump's resort unnecessary.

Weighing it up: Russia has said it will attend at a high level, and Lavrov is the natural choice either way. Against that, the US venue is unusual. Russia may also send a lower-level delegation to avoid giving the summit too much weight, or to skip it if talks sour. In 2022 and 2023 Lavrov attended in person while Putin did not, and he has just travelled to the US. On the other hand, in Bali and Delhi Lavrov's presence was assured by the host country's friendliness. In Miami, Putin would be the one the US wants, and if he decides to go, Lavrov goes too. If Putin skips, Lavrov is still the most probable representative, though he might be replaced by Overchuk or others, since Lavrov already did the Atlanta trip. I estimate about 60–65%.
